title: Per-variant KV-slice and working-set sculpting for long-context models (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
creator: Asha Patel
body: Summary: Create per-model (Llama, Mistral, Qwen family) configurations for KV cache slicing, eviction heuristics, and working-set sculpting to reduce GPU memory fragmentation and lower resident footprint for long-context scenarios while preserving latency SLOs. This ticket captures the design, experiments, and rollout plan for per-variant tuning that integrates with the continuous batching pipeline and the allocator.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For each target model variant (Llama-2-70B, Mistral-Base-65B, Qwen-72B longctx), document a KV-slice & residency config that reduces peak GPU resident memory by at least 10% vs current default without increasing 95th percentile token latency by >5%. 2) Configuration can be selected automatically by the runtime based on model metadata. 3) Integration tests demonstrating correct KV eviction and no cache corruption. 4) Canary rollout to 10% of production traffic with monitoring dashboards and rollback playbook.
implementation_notes:
- Add per-model KV-slice profiles in model catalog metadata.
- Implement a lightweight runtime selector: use model name + context-length hint to pick slice size, prefetch window, and eviction watermark.
- Extend allocator hooks to support soft-residency tiers (hot/warm/cold) for KV shards.
- Ensure continuous batching still coalesces requests with mixed slice settings by normalizing to a serving slice and applying per-request migration penalties.
- Provide a config override for Dedicated customers.
- Feature flag guarded: kv_variant_profiles_v1.
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1286 (runtime selector), github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/47 (residency tiers).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for profile selection and fallback.
- Synthetic load tests with 1k concurrent chat sessions at long context (32k tokens) per model variant.
- End-to-end perf runs on p4d and A100 80GB with mixed batch sizes (1, 4, 16).
- Regression tests to confirm KV integrity across evictions (checksum comparison).
- Canary plan: start with internal sandbox -> staging -> 10% production -> 50% -> full.
- Monitoring: token latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, out-of-memory signals, cache hit rate, model-specific cost per token dashboard.
benchmarks:
Initial spike results (sandbox, quantized weights):
- Qwen-72B longctx: peak resident down 14% (baseline 78.1GB -> 67.1GB), P95 token latency +1.8%.
- Llama-2-70B longctx: peak resident down 11%, P95 token latency +2.6%.
- Mistral-Base-65B: peak resident down 9%, P95 token latency +1.2%.
Notes: Qwen showed highest wins due to larger KV shard redundancy; Mistral required more conservative eviction to avoid regen overhead.
Test artifacts: perf-run-2025-02-28.json (link below).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag enabled in staging with detailed dashboards. 2) Canary 10% traffic for non-critical tenants for 48 hours; monitor OOM and tail latency; roll back on >3 sigma latency regression or any OOM. 3) Expand to 50% for 1 week. 4) Promote to all hosted models and include as default for Dedicated customers with opt-out. 5) Publish model profile docs and release notes.
notes_and_tradeoffs:
- Trade-off: aggressive slicing reduces peak memory but can increase recompute/regeneration latency when evicting hot KV. We plan to favor modest spill thresholds for Llama and more aggressive residency for Qwen.
- Mixed-variant batching introduces normalization overhead; we will benchmark the threshold where normalization costs outweigh memory wins.
- Dedicated customers with strict SLAs may opt to pin a higher residency quota.
- This work does not change quantization path; combined wins expected when paired with 4-bit kernels in runtime-1.21.
